Add tool-based retrieval evaluation axis
description: The framework only tests static context injection (dump all docs into prompt). Real agents use tools like grep, glob, read_file to search docs on-demand. Add a new retrieval-strategy axis with levels like: full-injection, search-then-read, summary-then-drill, rag-embedding. Requires: tool definitions in prompts, actual tool execution during trials, metrics on retrieval quality (tool calls needed, relevance of retrieved content). This is the single biggest gap — at realistic doc sizes, tool-based retrieval should massively outperform context injection.

title: Add multi-turn conversation support to evaluation framework
description: All 355 tasks are single-turn (one prompt → one response). Real agents have multi-turn conversations where they search, read results, refine queries, and iterate. Need: multi-turn task definitions, conversation history management, context decay measurement (docs injected at turn 1 getting compressed by turn 50), iterative refinement scoring. Affects: task base class, runner, LLMClient, scoring functions.

title: Run Taguchi screening against real documentation datasets
description: Current 177K-trial screening uses only the synthetic 56-file/9.4K-token fixture. Results won't generalize. The framework already has 11 dataset adapters (repliqa, swe_bench, code_rag_bench, etc.) but they haven't been prepared or used. Need to: prepare at least 2-3 real datasets, run screening against them, validate that Taguchi factor rankings are consistent across datasets. If rankings differ, the framework needs dataset-conditional recommendations.

title: Replace regex tool scoring with actual tool execution in agentic tasks
description: The agentic task type only regex-matches tool names in response text. 'I would call grep_files' scores the same as actually calling it. Need: provide real tool definitions to the LLM (OpenAI tool_use / Claude tool_use), execute tool calls against the doc corpus, score based on actual retrieval quality and execution results, support multi-step tool chains. Currently in agentic.py _score_tool_usage() does text pattern matching only.

title: Add prompt caching evaluation to framework
description: Some doc formats cache better than others with Anthropic's prompt caching (90% cost savings on cache hits). The framework doesn't measure or optimize for cacheability. Need: track cache hit rates per variant, measure cost with/without caching, potentially add a caching-friendliness axis. Stable system message prefixes cache better — format choices that keep the doc index stable across tasks would score higher.

title: Add context competition testing (docs vs code vs history)
description: Real agents have code, conversation history, tool results, AND docs competing for context space. The framework tests docs in isolation — the system message is basically just the rendered index. Need: simulate realistic context budgets where docs must share space with code snippets, prior conversation turns, and tool output. Measure how format choices degrade when docs get only 30% of available context vs 100%.

title: Models page premium polish
Make variant rendering task-aware
description: render(doc_tree) doesn't know what task is being asked. A retrieval task and a code generation task get the same rendered output. Real doc systems surface different content depending on the query. Need: pass task context to render(), allow variants to adapt output based on task type/question, measure whether task-aware rendering outperforms static rendering. Affects IndexVariant.render() signature and CompositeVariant.

title: Measure axis interaction effects in Taguchi analysis
description: The Taguchi L50 design assumes axes are independent (additivity assumption). But interactions likely exist — e.g., granularity × scale (file-level is fine at 5 files but terrible at 200), format × metadata (YAML format may benefit more from rich metadata than markdown-list). Need: run follow-up experiments with interaction columns in the OA, or use full factorial on top-K factors (the refinement phase partially addresses this). Add interaction effect detection to the analysis module.

title: Add train/test split for generalization testing
description: All 355 gold tasks are used for both tuning and evaluation — no held-out test set. Results may not generalize to unseen tasks. Need: split gold tasks into train (for Taguchi screening) and test (for validation), or use cross-validation. Also need cross-corpus validation: train on synthetic fixture, test on real datasets. Currently all tasks in gold_standard/ are used together.

title: Validate task difficulty labels empirically
description: Tasks are labeled easy/medium/hard/edge but labels are never validated. Need: compute empirical difficulty from baseline variant scores, build difficulty curves per variant, detect variants that fail on easy tasks (regression) vs variants that handle hard tasks well (ceiling effects). Use the oracle and no-docs baselines to calibrate. Currently difficulty is just a metadata label with no scoring impact.

title: Add structured output scoring (JSON, code AST, schemas)
description: All scoring is text-based (keyword matching, regex, fuzzy string comparison). No JSON schema validation, no deep AST-level code comparison beyond basic syntax checks. Need: JSON mode / structured output support in LLMClient, schema-based scoring for code_generation and fact_extraction tasks, Pydantic model validation scoring. Would enable testing whether certain doc formats produce more parseable/structured agent responses.

title: Fix robustness tasks missing base_task_id metadata
description: All 30 robustness task YAML files have the base_task_id field but it is set to empty string ('') rather than linking to the actual base task. The field exists in metadata but contains no useful data, breaking traceability — cannot link robustness tasks back to their base fact_extraction/retrieval tasks to measure perturbation impact. Need to populate base_task_id with the actual source task ID for each robustness task.

title: Fix variant teardown not called when continue_on_error=False
description: When continue_on_error=False and a trial raises an exception, variant.teardown() is never called. Variants with cleanup (e.g., temp files, search indexes) leak resources. The teardown call should be in a finally block. Affects runner.py trial execution loop. Known issue documented in MEMORY.md.

title: Fix CompositeVariant header duplication on concatenation
description: CompositeVariant concatenates axis outputs with newline separator. When two format variants both output markdown headers (e.g., '# Documentation Index'), the result has duplicate headers that break markdown table parsing. Affected variants: format_markdown_table.py, format_yaml.py, format_markdown_list.py. Fix: either strip headers before concatenation or deduplicate them in CompositeVariant.render().

title: Apply Bonferroni/BH correction to Taguchi factor p-values
description: Taguchi ANOVA computes raw p-values for each factor but does NOT apply multiple comparisons correction. With 10 factors at alpha=0.05, expected false positive rate is ~40%. benjamini_hochberg() exists in statistics.py but is never called from analysis.py. Factor significance claims are statistically invalid without correction. Quick fix: apply BH correction to p-values before reporting significance in compute_main_effects/run_anova.

title: Handle bimodal/binary LLM scores in S/N ratio computation
description: LLM evaluation scores are bounded [0,1] and often bimodal (many 0s and 1s). The S/N ratio formula for larger_is_better uses mean(1/y^2) which goes to infinity for y=0. Current epsilon guard (1e-10) masks the degeneracy. ANOVA F-test assumes normality which is violated by bimodal data. Need: data transformation (arcsine/logit), non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis fallback, or document actual score distributions before claiming statistical significance.

title: Phase A: Table full width
Validate additivity assumption before Taguchi optimal prediction
description: predict_optimal() uses additive model (predicted = grand_mean + sum of effects) assuming zero interactions between factors. This is NOT validated. LLM scores likely have interactions (e.g., format x metadata, granularity x scale). Prediction errors of 5-20% are plausible if interactions are large. Need: interaction test on top factors, or at minimum document the assumption and warn in reports. Prediction interval SE is also under-conservative.

title: Fix efficiency task token counting to use real tokenizer
description: efficiency.py line 101 uses len(response.split()) to approximate token count for budget penalty. Word splitting is inaccurate: 'hello-world' counts as 1 word but 2-3 tokens, punctuation attached to words miscounted. Should use tiktoken or litellm's token_counter for accurate counting. Affects efficiency task score accuracy.

title: Add modern LLM refusal patterns to negative task scorer
description: negative.py has 35+ refusal phrases but misses modern patterns: 'I don't have access to', 'I'm unable to provide', 'I can't determine', 'no reliable information'. Modern Claude/GPT refusals using these phrases score 0.0 (hallucination) instead of 1.0 (firm refusal). Add missing patterns to FIRM_REFUSAL_PHRASES and HEDGE_PHRASES lists.
close_reason: Fix verified: 2 reviewer approvals + CodeRabbit PASS. Commit b0440e1.

title: Normalize Unicode diacritics in fact extraction scorer
description: Fuzzy matching in fact_extraction.py fails on accented characters: 'cafe' vs 'café' scores 75 (below 85 threshold), giving 0.7 instead of 1.0. Same for 'naive'/'naïve', 'resume'/'résumé'. Fix: pre-normalize Unicode using unicodedata.normalize('NFD') + strip combining characters before fuzzy matching.
close_reason: Fix verified: 2 reviewer approvals + CodeRabbit PASS. Commit 60dd076.

title: Add input validation to EvalRunConfig
description: EvalRunConfig is a plain dataclass with no validation. Invalid configs silently accepted: repetitions=0 (no trials run), max_connections=-1 (undefined ThreadPoolExecutor behavior), temperature=-0.5 (API rejects), output_format='invalid' (no output written, no error). Should use Pydantic or add __post_init__ validation. Errors currently surface far from source during execution.

title: Add missing metrics to TaguchiRunner (scoring_ms, prompt_build_ms, judge)
description: TaguchiRunner (taguchi/runner.py) only records oa_row_id, phase, api_call_ms, total_api_ms, retry_count in trial metrics. Missing compared to EvalRunner: scoring_ms, prompt_build_ms, judge_score, judge_heuristic_delta. Users comparing Taguchi vs full-sweep results see different metric sets. Should harmonize both runners.

title: Upgrade silent judge failures from DEBUG to WARNING
description: runner.py line ~750: LLM-as-judge failures are caught with bare except and logged at DEBUG level only. If judge calls fail consistently (rate limited, model unavailable), users won't notice. judge_score metric silently missing from affected trials. Should log at WARNING level and track failure count in DiagnosticTracker.

title: Optimize TaguchiRunner to setup/teardown once per OA row instead of per trial
description: TaguchiRunner creates a new CompositeVariant and calls setup()/teardown() for EVERY trial (taguchi/runner.py lines 266-268, 343-344). For 177,500 trials with 10 axes, that is 1.77M setup/teardown calls. Most variants have no-op setup/teardown, but any variant with real work (disk I/O, preprocessing) suffers. Should group trials by OA row and setup/teardown once per row.

title: Add database indexes to observatory store for query performance
description: Observatory store.py trials table has no secondary indexes. Missing: composite index on (run_id, task_type, variant_name), index on (source, task_type), index on (variant_name, repetition). At 177K+ trials, queries for web dashboard filtering and report aggregation will be slow. Add indexes in schema migration.

title: Add pytest-cov coverage tracking to CI pipeline
description: CI pipeline (.github/workflows/quality-checks.yml) runs linting and security checks but does NOT run tests with coverage measurement. No coverage threshold enforcement. Should add pytest-cov to CI with 80% minimum threshold per CLAUDE.md requirements. Currently 1744+ tests exist but no coverage reporting.
close_reason: Added pytest-cov, coverage config, and CI workflow. Current coverage 94%. Commit b746816.

title: Phase A: Checkbox animate-out
Add SD, CI, and median to report aggregation
description: reports/aggregator.py only computes mean score per group. Missing: standard deviation, standard error, confidence intervals, median, percentiles. bootstrap_ci() exists in statistics.py but is never called from aggregation. Two variants with means 0.73 vs 0.74 can't be compared without variability estimates. Should add SD, 95% CI, and median to VariantSummary.
close_reason: Added std_dev, median, ci_lower, ci_upper to VariantSummary. _summarize() computes all fields. 6 new tests. Commit 5bccaef.

title: Add JSON error handling in observatory get_phase_results()
description: observatory/store.py get_phase_results() calls json.loads() on 4 columns without error handling. If corrupted JSON is stored in the database, function raises unhandled JSONDecodeError and crashes. Database becomes unusable. Add try/except with fallback to None and WARNING log for corrupted fields.

title: Validate non-empty axes before building Taguchi design in pipeline
description: pipeline.py run_screening() builds axes dict from variants but doesn't validate it has at least 2 axes with 2+ levels each. If variants is empty or all variants are axis 0 (baseline), build_design() receives empty/minimal axes dict and will fail or produce a trivial design. Add validation before calling build_design().

title: Remove dead code duplication in pipeline.py refinement phase
description: pipeline.py run_refinement() has if axes: / else: branches (lines 260-289) that both call self._orchestrator.run() with identical parameters. The if/else is dead code duplication. Collapse into a single call.

title: Fix dataset adapters silently returning empty on load errors
description: Multiple dataset adapters (e.g., ibm_techqa.py) catch broad Exception and return empty list on HuggingFace load failures. Caller cannot distinguish 'no data' from 'error loading data'. This silently corrupts evaluation runs — user thinks dataset has 0 tasks when it actually failed to download. Should raise or log at WARNING with clear error context.

title: Add file size limits and streaming to agent-index scanner
description: agent-index scanner.py loads entire file contents into memory via Path.read_text(). For documentation suites with multi-megabyte generated API docs, this could cause memory problems. No max file size checks, no streaming support, no warnings for large files. Add configurable max_file_size with warning/skip for oversized files.

title: Add retry logic and auth support to agent-index GitHub scanner
description: agent-index scanner.py GitHub scanner detects 403 rate limits but provides no retry mechanism. No exponential backoff, no authentication support (unauthenticated gets 60 req/hour). Large repos quickly hit rate limits. Add: GITHUB_TOKEN env var support, exponential backoff with jitter, configurable max retries.

title: Update MEMORY.md: remove false known issues (fnmatch, validate.py)
description: MEMORY.md lists two agent-index known issues that audit found are NOT issues: (1) fnmatch.fnmatch allows * to match / — actually uses _simple_glob_to_regex() which correctly prevents this. (2) validate.py and autodetect.py use absolute item.parts — actually uses item.relative_to(root).parts. Remove these false entries from MEMORY.md known issues.
close_reason: MEMORY.md updated: removed false known issues (fnmatch, validate.py, TrialResult.metrics). No code commit - auto-memory directory.

title: Establish consistent error handling strategy across codebase
description: Audit found inconsistent error handling: some modules swallow all exceptions and return defaults (datasets/), some log at DEBUG and continue (runner.py judge), some log at WARNING and raise (llm/client.py), some silently return None/empty (observatory/tracker.py). Need policy: external data sources (HF, APIs) → return None/empty + log WARNING; internal logic errors → log ERROR + raise; optional features (judge) → log WARNING + skip.

title: Fix GitHub cache path collision from slash-to-underscore replacement
Phase A: Animated counts
Fix validate.py using hardcoded extensions/ignore patterns instead of config
description: In validate.py, _collect_disk_files() hardcodes extensions={.md,.mdx,.rst,.txt} and ignore_dirs={node_modules,__pycache__,.git,.venv} instead of using the config's file_extensions and ignore_patterns. If a user configures custom extensions (e.g. .adoc) or custom ignore patterns, validation reports false positives: scanned files appear as 'missing' and actual disk files are missed as 'extra'. Fix: pass file_extensions and ignore_patterns from config into _collect_disk_files and validate_index.

title: Fix inject_into_file not writing markers on new file creation
description: In output.py inject_into_file(), when the target file doesn't exist (line 323-324), it writes just the raw content without wrapping it in START/END markers. On subsequent runs, the function can't find markers and appends the content again, causing duplication. Fix: wrap the content with markers when creating a new file, so subsequent runs can replace the content idempotently.

title: Fix algorithmic_compress stripping injection markers (HTML comments)
description: In transform.py, algorithmic_compress() removes ALL HTML comments via re.sub(r'<\!--.*?-->', '', content, flags=re.DOTALL). This strips injection markers like <\!-- DOCS:START --> and <\!-- DOCS:END --> used by inject_into_file(). If someone runs the transform pipeline on a file that uses these markers, the markers are destroyed, breaking the injection system. Fix: either exclude marker-pattern comments from stripping, or document this as a known interaction and ensure the pipeline doesn't operate on files with injection markers.

title: Fix cursor rules YAML frontmatter not properly escaped
description: In output.py render_cursor_rules(), the YAML frontmatter is constructed via f-strings without proper YAML escaping: f'description: {tier_config.instruction}' and f'globs: {globs}'. If tier_config.instruction contains YAML-special characters (colons, brackets, quotes), the frontmatter becomes invalid YAML. Similarly, if file paths in globs contain commas or special chars, the glob list is misinterpreted. Fix: use yaml.dump or quote the values properly.

title: Remove unused index_content parameter from validate_index()
description: In validate.py, validate_index() accepts an index_content: str parameter that is never used in the function body. The docstring claims it's 'used to extract referenced paths' but the code only uses doc_tree.files.keys(). This is dead code that confuses the API. Either remove the parameter or implement the documented behavior.

title: Fix local scanner size_bytes inconsistency with GitHub scanner
description: In scanner.py _create_docfile(), size_bytes is set from stat.st_size (raw disk bytes), while the GitHub scanner computes len(content.encode('utf-8')). On Windows, text mode reading converts CRLF to LF, so stat.st_size > len(content.encode('utf-8')). This inconsistency means size_bytes has different semantics depending on the source. Fix: use len(content.encode('utf-8')) in the local scanner too, matching the GitHub scanner and the actual content that content_hash is computed from.

title: Fix overly broad exception catch in autodetect _detect_project_name
description: In autodetect.py line 167, except (OSError, Exception) is equivalent to except Exception, swallowing all errors including unexpected ones like AttributeError or TypeError. This hides real bugs during project name detection from pyproject.toml. Fix: catch specific exceptions (OSError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError, KeyError).

title: Fix pipeline confirmation phase hardcoded predicted_sn=0.0
description: In pipeline.py lines 206-209, run_confirmation() creates OptimalPrediction with predicted_sn=0.0 hardcoded instead of using the actual predicted_sn from the screening phase. This makes confirmation validation meaningless - sigma_deviation will be wrong, and within_interval uses a fallback interval instead of checking against the real prediction.

title: Fix thread-unsafe variant setup for Oracle/LMR baselines in EvalRunner
description: In runner.py _setup_variant_for_task() (lines 567-590), OracleBaseline and LengthMatchedRandomBaseline instances have their state mutated via set_relevant_docs()/set_target_tokens() from concurrent threads in ThreadPoolExecutor. These baseline variants store task-specific state as instance attributes (_relevant_docs, _target_tokens in baselines.py), so concurrent trials can overwrite each other's state, leading to incorrect scoring results.

title: Fix DiagnosticTracker snapshot averages diluted by resume offset
description: In diagnostics.py, when resuming a run, _completed starts at completed_offset but _total_api_ms/_total_trial_ms only accumulate from new trials. The snapshot() method computes avg_api_ms = total_new_api_ms / (offset + new_count), which dilutes the averages since the denominator includes previously-completed trials but the numerator only has timing data from new trials.

title: Phase B: Dual-handle range slider
Fix beam_search within_parity flags not updated after Holm-Bonferroni
description: In beam_search.py select_beam() (lines 148-189), candidate.within_parity flags are set based on raw p-values BEFORE the Holm-Bonferroni correction is applied at lines 188-189. After correction, the pairwise_tests list gets updated p-values but the candidate flags still reflect the uncorrected values. This can cause candidates to be incorrectly marked as within parity when their corrected p-values would reject the null hypothesis.
